What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the right. The parabola has its vertex at $(0,0)$ and passes through the point $(12,4).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(0,0)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Since we know the given parabola passes through the point $(12,4),$ we can substitute $x=12$ and $y=4$ into the standard equation and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ {4}^{2} & =4p(12) \\ 16 & =48p \\ p & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ {y}^{2} & =4(\frac{1}{3})x \\ {y}^{2} & =\frac{4}{3}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the right since $p=\frac{1}{3}$ is positive.

\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4p(x+1) \\ (6-2)^{2} & =4p(-2+1) \\ 16 & =-4p \\ p & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4p(x+1) \\ (y-2)^{2} & =4(-4)(x+1) \\ (y-2)^{2} & =-16(x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the equation of the left-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(4,-3)$ and passes through the point $(1,0).$
questions.worked_solution:
The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(4,-3),$ we substitute $h=4$ and $k=-3$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+3)^{2} & =4p(x-4).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(1,0),$ so we can substitute $x=1$ and $y=0$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+3)^{2} & =4p(x-4) \\ (0+3)^{2} & =4p(1-4) \\ 9 & =-12p \\ p & =-\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+3)^{2} & =4p(x-4) \\ (y+3)^{2} & =4(-\frac{3}{4})(x-4) \\ (y+3)^{2} & =-3(x-4).\end{aligned}
$$
